```{python}
import sys

from shared.components import chart_card, method_and_sources, prev_next, stat_tile, stat_tiles
from shared.context import load_context
from shared.outputs import read_output
from shared.paths import CASE_STUDIES, REPO_URL, ROOT

STUDY = CASE_STUDIES / "03_road_casualties"
sys.path.insert(0, str(STUDY / "analysis"))
import figures as F  # noqa: E402

roads, prov_roads, notes_roads = read_output(STUDY / "outputs" / "road_casualties.csv")
avg, prov_avg, notes_avg = read_output(STUDY / "outputs" / "road_periods.csv")
check, prov_check, notes_check = read_output(STUDY / "outputs" / "road_crosscheck.csv")
ctx = load_context(STUDY / "context.yml")  # news and journals, background only (policy §7)

FIRST, LAST = int(roads.year.min()), int(roads.year.max())
y = roads.set_index("year")
# Period figures from the counts, not the rounded averages, to avoid double rounding.
P1, P2, P3 = avg.period.tolist()


def period(p, col):
    a, b = (int(v) for v in p.split("–"))
    return y.loc[a:b, col].mean()


def per(p, col, unit):
    a, b = (int(v) for v in p.split("–"))
    return y.loc[a:b, col].sum() / y.loc[a:b, "accidents"].sum() * unit


def num(v):
    return f"{v:,.0f}"


def signed(v, d=0):
    return f"{v:+.{d}f}%".replace("-", "−")


def size(v, d=0):
    """Size of a rise or fall for prose ("fell 27%"), where the verb carries the sign."""
    return f"{abs(v):.{d}f}%"


def change(a, b):
    return (b / a - 1) * 100


acc1, acc2, acc3 = (period(p, "accidents") for p in (P1, P2, P3))
inj1, inj2, inj3 = (period(p, "injuries") for p in (P1, P2, P3))
dth1, dth2, dth3 = (period(p, "deaths") for p in (P1, P2, P3))
ipa1, ipa3 = per(P1, "injuries", 100), per(P3, "injuries", 100)
dpa1, dpa2, dpa3 = (per(p, "deaths", 1000) for p in (P1, P2, P3))
step = {c: change(y.loc[2011, c], y.loc[2012, c]) for c in ("accidents", "injuries", "deaths")}
dmin, dmax = y.deaths.min(), y.deaths.max()
dmin_year, dmax_year = y.deaths.idxmin(), y.deaths.idxmax()
inj_2017_high = y.loc[2012:2017, "injuries"].idxmax() == 2017
```

::: {.study-intro}
This case study looks at **road accidents recorded by the Royal Brunei Police Force from
2009 to 2017**, and the people injured and killed in them. Because single years swing a lot,
it compares three 3-year periods: 2009–2011, 2012–2014 and 2015–2017. The data ends in 2017,
although it was published in 2025. It shows **what changed and when, not why**.

It asks two questions, answered in the conclusion:

1. **Did road accidents, injuries and deaths go up or down from 2009 to 2017?**
2. **Did accidents become less likely to injure or kill?**
:::

```{python}
stat_tiles(
    stat_tile(f"People killed a year, {P3}", num(dth3), signed(change(dth1, dth3)), f"vs {P1} ({num(dth1)} a year)"),
    stat_tile(f"People injured a year, {P3}", num(inj3), signed(change(inj1, inj3)), f"vs {P1} ({num(inj1)} a year)"),
    stat_tile(f"Accidents a year, {P3}", num(acc3), signed(change(acc1, acc3)), f"vs {P1} ({num(acc1)} a year)"),
)
```

```{python}
fig, table = F.overview(roads, avg)
chart_card(
    fig,
    title="Accidents held steady while injuries and deaths stepped down after 2011",
    subtitle=f"Accidents, people injured and people killed per year · {FIRST}–{LAST} · dotted lines: 3-year averages",
    alt=(
        f"Three line charts. Accidents stay between {num(y.accidents.min())} and "
        f"{num(y.accidents.max())} a year. People injured average {num(inj1)} a year in {P1}, "
        f"then {num(inj2)} and {num(inj3)}. People killed average {num(dth1)}, then "
        f"{num(dth2)} and {num(dth3)}."
    ),
    provenance=prov_roads,
    table=table,
    height=340,
    mobile_fig=F.overview(roads, avg, cols=1)[0],
    mobile_height=760,
)
```

## Accidents, injuries and deaths, 2009–2017

The police recorded between `{python} num(y.accidents.min())` and
`{python} num(y.accidents.max())` road accidents a year. The 3-year averages barely moved:
`{python} num(acc1)`, `{python} num(acc2)` and `{python} num(acc3)` a year.

The number of people hurt did change. People injured averaged `{python} num(inj1)` a year in
`{python} P1`, then `{python} num(inj2)` and `{python} num(inj3)`. People killed averaged
`{python} num(dth1)` a year, then `{python} num(dth2)` and `{python} num(dth3)`.

## The step down in 2012

Most of the fall happened in a single year. From 2011 to 2012, injuries fell
`{python} size(step["injuries"])` and deaths `{python} size(step["deaths"])`, while accidents
fell `{python} size(step["accidents"])`. Both then stayed near their new level.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="What was reported at the time"}
These come from published articles and studies, not from the data above.

- **Before the step.** A 2011 study reported that road deaths in Brunei had been rising
  since 2003. It linked this to lax enforcement of traffic laws, more young drivers and more
  new vehicles, and recommended the "Safe System" approach to road safety
  (`{python} ctx["haque2011"].cite()`).
- **May 2011.** The Brunei Darussalam Road Safety Council launched a ten-year *Blueprint Decade
  of Action for Road Safety 2011–2020*, with programmes to run with other agencies
  (`{python} ctx["mohamad2011"].cite()`).
- **A later evaluation.** A 2018 study reported a 30% fall in deaths and serious injuries in
  the first 12 months after Brunei introduced reformed road safety initiatives, which it calls
  the Road Safety System Approach. Its summary doesn't give the start date
  (`{python} ctx["haque2018"].cite()`).

These reports come from around the time of the step, but they don't show that any of them
caused it. The data doesn't say why the step happened, and a change in how injuries and deaths
were recorded is also possible. Fire and Rescue's figures, used here as a check, only start in
2012, so they can't confirm it either way.
:::

## Deaths year by year, 2009–2017

Road deaths varied from `{python} num(dmin)` (`{python} dmin_year`) to `{python} num(dmax)`
(`{python} dmax_year`) a year. With numbers this small, one year's change says little: a
single serious crash can move the total. The 3-year averages give a steadier picture.

```{python}
fig, table = F.deaths(roads, avg)
chart_card(
    fig,
    title=f"Road deaths ranged from {num(dmin)} to {num(dmax)} a year; the 3-year average fell from {num(dth1)} to {num(dth3)}",
    subtitle=f"People killed in road accidents per year · {FIRST}–{LAST} · lines: 3-year averages",
    alt=(
        f"Bar chart of road deaths per year, from {num(dmin)} in {dmin_year} to {num(dmax)} in "
        f"{dmax_year}, with 3-year averages of {num(dth1)}, {num(dth2)} and {num(dth3)}."
    ),
    provenance=prov_roads,
    table=table,
)
```

## Injuries and deaths per accident, 2009–2017

Because accidents held steady while injuries fell, each accident injured fewer people on
average: `{python} f"{ipa1:.1f}"` people per 100 accidents in `{python} P1`, against
`{python} f"{ipa3:.1f}"` in `{python} P3`. Deaths per 1,000 accidents fell from
`{python} f"{dpa1:.1f}"` to `{python} f"{dpa2:.1f}"` and `{python} f"{dpa3:.1f}"`.

```{python}
fig, table = F.per_accident(roads, avg)
chart_card(
    fig,
    title=f"About {ipa3:.0f} people were injured per 100 accidents after 2011, down from about {ipa1:.0f}",
    subtitle=f"People injured per 100 recorded accidents · {FIRST}–{LAST} · dotted lines: 3-year averages",
    alt=(
        f"Line chart of people injured per 100 accidents: about 20 from {FIRST} to 2011, then "
        f"between {y.loc[2012:, 'injuries_per_100_accidents'].min():.0f} and "
        f"{y.loc[2012:, 'injuries_per_100_accidents'].max():.0f} from 2012 to {LAST}."
    ),
    provenance=prov_roads,
    table=table,
)
```

## Conclusion

- **Did road accidents, injuries and deaths go up or down from 2009 to 2017?** Accidents held
  steady (`{python} num(acc1)` a year in `{python} P1`, `{python} num(acc3)` in
  `{python} P3`). Injuries and deaths fell by about a quarter between the same periods
  (`{python} signed(change(inj1, inj3))` and `{python} signed(change(dth1, dth3))`), mostly in
  one step in 2012. After that they stayed near the same level`{python} ", and 2017 had the most injuries since 2011" if inj_2017_high else ""`.
- **Did accidents become less likely to injure or kill?** As recorded, yes: people injured per
  100 accidents fell from `{python} f"{ipa1:.1f}"` to `{python} f"{ipa3:.1f}"`, and people
  killed per 1,000 accidents from `{python} f"{dpa1:.1f}"` to `{python} f"{dpa3:.1f}"`.

::: {.callout-caution appearance="simple" title="What this doesn't tell us"}
<!-- Side note: required on every case study (DESIGN.md §4.1). -->
- **Road safety today.** The latest year published is `{python} LAST`.
- **Why.** Road safety initiatives were reported around 2011 (see "What was reported at the
  time"), but neither they nor the data show what caused the 2012 step. It may also be a change
  in recording.
- **How serious.** The source doesn't define an injury (serious or slight) or a road death
  (for example, within 30 days of the crash).
- **Who and where.** There are no districts, road users (drivers, passengers, pedestrians,
  motorcyclists), ages or times of day.
- **Rates per person or vehicle.** These are counts. Brunei's population and number of
  vehicles changed over these years, and the counts aren't adjusted for that.
:::
